packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: My context contained general project notes (a fragment-identification
project at a monastic archive, batch names) but no proposed identification, author, work
title or prior transcription for these images. Nothing in my context names the text on
this leaf. I did not search, consult editions or open anything beyond PROMPT.md and the
image files. I did list the packet directory (packet.json is present; I did not open it).
Personal names below (symon, faustinianus, petrus, clemens, aquila, niceta, etc.) are
read from the images, not supplied; I make no identification.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY
======================================================================
Two faces, each shown in a reduced overview: image-001 (face A, exterior of a binding
wrapper; pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 122r") and image-014 (face B, interior; pencil
"... Frg. 122v"). Tiles: image-002..013 cover face A (3 rows x 4), image-015..026 cover
face B (3 rows x 4). Tiles overlap.

Face A (image-001): a bifolium-sized piece reused as a cover, folded with a spine area
in the middle. Two blocks of manuscript text, one each side of the spine fold, each a
single column of long lines, Gothic textualis, brown ink, red paragraph marks (¶) and red
strokes on some capitals. Left block: about 30 lines, lower third blank (end of text or
lower margin). Right block: about 30 lines, overwritten across lines 3-6 by a large
later (early modern) title in black ink: "Mittl(?) Hellner(?) Anschlo(?) / Urbarium /
[fu]i 1661:62:63:64:65: et 1666", and a blue-bordered oval paper label "III / 61".
Stamp "Stiftsarchiv Stams" below right block. Later cursive notes in the top margin
above the left block (image-003, three lines, illegible to me: "...z.t.601 ... 103: t: z
..."). A separate strip of text visible at the top edge of each block (folded-over
flaps; image-003 top right and image-004 top) belongs to the other face or a turn-in.
Left-margin numeral "10" (?) beside left block line 8 (image-002) and a marginal "fum"
(?) beside a lower line (image-006). Small horizontal pen strokes in the right margin of
the left block (image-007) look like line ticks or ruling marks.

Face B (image-014): left half largely covered by adhered printed paper waste (black-letter
print, much of it in mirror-image offset, red-printed initials; words like "Oratio",
"remissionis", "bonitatem tuam", "numerum arene maris", "de peccatorum", "Solent delicte"
visible in print). This printed material is NOT the manuscript and I did not transcribe it
beyond these notes. Manuscript text survives on face B in two areas: lower part of the
left block (image-019/020/023/024, about 10 lines) and most of the right block
(image-017/018/021/022/025/026, about 36 lines, heavily stained, top lines lost under
adhered paper). Red paragraph marks and red-touched capitals.

Interpretation (tentative): continuous narrative prose, not text-plus-commentary. No
glosses or lemmata seen. Right block of face A and the left block of face B are in the
same hand as the others.

Selected spans: face A left block (nearly complete), face A right block (lines below the
later title), face B right block (lines 1-36), face B left block lower 10 lines.
Unread / poorly read: face A right block lines 1-6 (under the later title), face B left
block upper part (under printed paper), end-of-line words in face A right block where
stained, top flaps.

Conventions: (x) = expansion; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible]; [...] = text runs
off tile or is lost; line numbers are counted from the top of the named image, counting
manuscript text lines only.
